title.zh: 位次之争：廉颇的委屈与那根荆条
title.en: The Quarrel Over Rank: Lian Po's Grievance and the Bundle of Thorns

dek.zh: 蔺相如从渑池回来，因功拜为上卿，位在廉颇之上；廉颇有攻城野战之功，不服，扬言见面必辱之。相如处处避让，连门客都要辞去。这场僵局最后以廉颇肉袒负荆收场，而作者认为，这份不服并非全无来由。
dek.en: Back from the meeting at Mianchi, Lin Xiangru was made shangqing for his service and ranked above Lian Po, a general whose merit lay in cities stormed and battles won. Lian Po would not swallow it and swore he would humiliate him wherever they met. Lin Xiangru kept giving ground, until even his own retainers threatened to walk out. The standoff ended with Lian Po baring his back and carrying a bundle of thorns to beg forgiveness; and the author's view is that this grievance was not groundless.

paras.zh: 蔺相如从渑池回来，因功拜为上卿，位次排在廉颇之上。廉颇是赵国良将，伐齐取阳晋，以勇气闻名诸侯，他的态度很直接：蔺相如「徒以口舌爲勞」，凭什么位居我上。他公开放话，见了面就要羞辱对方。这件事难在，按他自己的说法，他有攻城野战之大功，而相如的功劳记在口舌上，两人同朝为上卿，一个要辱，一个在躲。
paras.en: Lin Xiangru came back from the meeting at Mianchi and was made shangqing, placed above Lian Po. Lian Po was a fine general of Zhao: he had beaten Qi, taken Yangjin and won a name for courage among the states. His reaction was blunt. Lin Xiangru had earned his place with nothing but his tongue; why should he sit above me? He announced that the next time they met he would humiliate the man. What makes the episode hard is that, by Lian Po's own account, he had great merit from storming cities and fighting in the field, while Lin Xiangru's credit was entered under words. Now both held the rank of shangqing at court: one meant to humiliate, the other hid.

heading.en: Where the Two Men Came From

paras.zh: 廉颇的资历是战场上打出来的：赵惠文王时为赵将伐齐，大破之，取阳晋，拜为上卿。蔺相如的来历则完全不同——他是赵国人，身份是宦者令缪贤的舍人，也就是门客。后来廉颇不服时，说的理由之一正是相如「素賤人」。
paras.en: Lian Po's credentials were earned on the battlefield. In the reign of King Huiwen of Zhao he commanded against Qi, routed it, seized Yangjin, and was raised to shangqing. Lin Xiangru's origins could hardly have been more different. He was a man of Zhao, and his standing was that of a sheren - a retainer in the service of Miao Xian, the head of the palace eunuchs. When Lian Po later refused to accept him, one of the reasons he gave was exactly this: the man had always been of low station.

paras.zh: 赵惠文王时，赵国得到楚国的和氏璧，秦昭王写信来，说愿用十五座城换它。赵王与大将军廉颇诸大臣商量，两头都难：给，怕城拿不到，白白被骗；不给，又怕秦兵打过来。主意定不下来，缺一个能去秦国回话的人。缪贤向赵王提起相如，讲了自己的一桩旧事：他曾有罪，私下打算逃去燕国，相如劝住他，理由是赵强燕弱、他正得宠于赵王，燕王当年示好正因为此，逃过去只会被捆着送回来；不如「肉袒伏斧質請罪」，倒还有活路。缪贤照做，赵王果然赦免了他。
paras.en: In King Huiwen's time Zhao acquired the Heshi jade from Chu, and King Zhaoxiang of Qin wrote offering fifteen cities for it. The king of Zhao consulted his great general Lian Po and the other ministers, and both answers looked bad: hand it over and the cities might never come, leaving Zhao cheated; refuse, and Qin's armies might come. Nothing was settled, and there was no one fit to carry the reply to Qin. Miao Xian brought up Lin Xiangru with the king, telling a story against himself. He had once been guilty of an offence and meant to flee to Yan. Lin Xiangru stopped him: Zhao was strong and Yan weak, and the king of Yan had courted Miao Xian only because he stood in the king of Zhao's favour; flee there, and Yan would tie him up and send him back. Better to bare his upper body, lie down at the executioner's block and ask pardon (to paraphrase the source) - there might still be a way to keep his life. Miao Xian did, and the king pardoned him.

paras.zh: 赵王召见相如，问他：秦王要用十五座城换我的璧，可以给吗？相如答：秦强而赵弱，不能不答应；秦以城求璧而赵不许，理亏在赵；赵给了璧而秦不给城，理亏在秦。「均之二策，甯許以負秦曲」——两相比较，宁可答应，让理亏落到秦国头上。赵王问谁可以出使，相如自请奉璧前往：城归赵，璧就留在秦；城不归赵，「臣請完璧歸趙」。赵王于是派相如奉璧西入秦国。
paras.en: The king summoned Lin Xiangru and asked him: the king of Qin wants to trade fifteen cities for my jade; may I give it? Lin Xiangru answered that Qin was strong and Zhao weak, so Zhao could not refuse. If Qin offers cities for the jade and Zhao refuses, the wrong is Zhao's; if Zhao hands over the jade and Qin refuses the cities, the wrong is Qin's. Weighing the two courses together, it is better to agree and leave Qin carrying the blame. When the king asked who could go as envoy, Lin Xiangru offered to carry the jade himself: if the cities came to Zhao, the jade would stay in Qin; if they did not, he would bring the jade back to Zhao intact. So the king sent Lin Xiangru west into Qin with the jade.

paras.zh: 到了秦廷，秦王在章台接见相如，接过璧大喜，传给身边的美人和侍从看，左右都高呼万岁。相如看出秦王无意偿城，上前说璧有小毛病要指给秦王看，拿到璧便退立倚柱，怒发上冲冠，当面斥责秦王，放话：大王若一定要逼我，「臣頭今與璧倶碎於柱矣」；直到此时才「持其璧睨柱，欲以撃柱」。秦王怕他砸碎，连忙道歉，召来主管官员查看地图，指着说从这里过去的十五座城给赵。相如判断这不过是做样子，城根本拿不到，于是说和氏璧是天下共传之宝，赵王送来前斋戒五日，秦王也该斋戒五日，设九宾于廷，他才敢献璧。秦王答应了，把他安置在广成传舍。相如断定秦王即便斋戒也一定违约，就让随从穿上粗布衣，把璧揣在怀里，从小路逃走，送回赵国。等再次上廷，他把话摊开：秦自缪公以来二十多位国君，没有一位说话算数；璧已送回赵国，「臣知欺大王之罪當誅，臣請就湯鑊」。秦王与群臣相视而嘻，左右有人要把他拉下去，秦王最终说，杀了相如也得不到璧，反而断了秦赵之好，不如以礼相待送他回去，「卒廷見相如，畢禮而歸之」。相如回国后，赵王认为他是贤大夫，出使不辱于诸侯，拜他为上大夫；而秦终究没有把城给赵，赵也始终没有把璧给秦。
paras.en: At the Qin court the king received Lin Xiangru in the Zhang Terrace, was delighted with the jade, and passed it around to his ladies and attendants, who all cried long life to him. Lin Xiangru saw he had no intention of paying. He said the gem had a small flaw he would point out, took it back and stood against a pillar, his hair bristling with anger, and denounced the king, warning that if the king insisted on pressing him, his head and the jade would be smashed together against the pillar. Only then did he stand holding the jade with his eyes on the pillar, ready to bring it down. The alarmed king apologised, summoned the officials concerned to consult the map and pointed out fifteen cities for Zhao. Lin Xiangru judged this mere show. The Heshi jade was a treasure the whole world talked of, he said; the king of Zhao had fasted five days before sending it, and the king of Qin should fast five days and hold the nine-fold ceremony at court before he would dare present it. The king agreed and lodged him at the Guangcheng hostel. Sure that the king would break his word even after fasting, Lin Xiangru had a follower put on coarse clothes, hide the jade in his robe and take it home to Zhao by back roads. At the next audience he laid it out: in more than twenty reigns since Duke Mu, Qin had never kept a firm agreement; the jade was already back in Zhao; he knew that deceiving the king was a crime deserving death, and he asked to be sent to the cauldron. The king and his ministers looked at one another and laughed wryly. Some attendants moved to drag him out, but the king reasoned that killing him would not bring back the jade and would end good relations with Zhao. In the end he received Lin Xiangru at court with full ceremony and sent him home. Once Lin Xiangru was back, the king of Zhao, judging him a worthy grandee who had not disgraced Zhao among the states, made him shangdafu. In the end Qin never handed the cities to Zhao, and Zhao never gave Qin the jade.

paras.zh: 此后秦国伐赵，攻下石城；第二年又攻赵，杀了二万人。秦王派使者告诉赵王，想在西河外的渑池与他相会修好。赵王畏秦，不想去；廉颇、蔺相如商议说：「王不行，示趙弱且怯也。」赵王于是赴会，相如随行。廉颇送王到边境，与赵王诀别时约定：算上路程和会面的礼节，往返不超过三十日；三十日不回，就请立太子为王，断掉秦国的念想。赵王答应了。到了渑池，秦王酒酣，请赵王鼓瑟，赵王鼓了，秦御史上前记下「某年月日，秦王與趙王會飲，令趙王鼓瑟」。相如上前，请秦王击缻以相娱乐，秦王发怒，不答应；相如捧缻上前，跪着请求，秦王仍不肯击。相如说：「五歩之内，相如請得以頸血濺大王矣！」秦王左右要拿刀杀相如，「相如張目叱之，左右皆靡」。秦王不高兴，只好击了一下缻，相如回头召赵御史记下：某年某月某日，秦王为赵王击缻。秦国群臣说，请以赵国十五座城为秦王祝寿；相如也说：「請以秦之咸陽爲趙王壽。」秦王直到酒宴结束，「終不能加勝於趙」；赵国也「盛設兵以待秦」，秦不敢动。
paras.en: After this Qin attacked Zhao and took Shicheng; the following year it attacked again and killed twenty thousand men. The king of Qin sent an envoy proposing a friendly meeting with the king of Zhao at Mianchi, beyond the Western River. The king of Zhao, afraid of Qin, wanted not to go, but Lian Po and Lin Xiangru advised that if the king stayed away it would show Zhao as weak and timid. So the king went, with Lin Xiangru in attendance. Lian Po escorted the king to the border and, taking leave, made an arrangement: allow for the road and the formalities of the meeting, and the round trip should take no more than thirty days; if the king was not back in thirty days, let the crown prince be set up as king, to cut off Qin's hopes. The king agreed. At Mianchi, when the wine was flowing, the king of Qin asked the king of Zhao to play the se, and he did; a Qin scribe stepped forward and recorded that on such a day the king of Qin, drinking with the king of Zhao, had ordered the king of Zhao to play the se. Lin Xiangru then came forward and asked the king of Qin to strike an earthen pot for their mutual entertainment. The king of Qin angrily refused. Lin Xiangru brought the pot forward, knelt and pressed him; still the king would not strike it. Lin Xiangru said that within five paces he could spatter the king with the blood from his own neck. The king's attendants moved to cut him down, but Lin Xiangru glared and shouted at them, and they all fell back. Displeased, the king of Qin struck the pot once, and Lin Xiangru turned and called the Zhao scribe to record that on such a day the king of Qin had struck the pot for the king of Zhao. Qin's ministers asked for fifteen cities of Zhao as a toast to the king of Qin's long life; Lin Xiangru asked in return for Qin's Xianyang as a toast to the king of Zhao's long life. To the end of the banquet the king of Qin could not gain the upper hand over Zhao; Zhao, for its part, had massed its forces to meet Qin, and Qin dared not move.

paras.zh: 回国以后，因相如功大，拜为上卿，位在廉颇之右。廉颇的话说得很白：「我爲趙將，有攻城野戰之大功，而藺相如徒以口舌爲勞，而位居我上，且相如素賤人，吾羞，不忍爲之下。」并且公开宣言：「我見相如，必辱之。」
paras.en: Back home, Lin Xiangru, for his great service, was made shangqing, ranked above Lian Po. Lian Po put it plainly: I am the general of Zhao, with great merit from storming cities and fighting in the field, while Lin Xiangru has labored only with his tongue and sits above me; and he has always been a man of low station. I am ashamed, and I cannot bear to stand beneath him. Then he declared openly: when I set eyes on Lin Xiangru, I will humiliate him.

paras.zh: 相如听说后，不肯与他相会。每逢朝会，常称病不去，不想同廉颇争位次的先后。出门远远望见廉颇，他就让自己的车避开躲起来。
paras.en: Lin Xiangru, hearing of it, refused to meet him. At court audiences he would often plead illness rather than jostle with Lian Po over precedence. When he did go out and caught sight of Lian Po in the distance, he turned his carriage aside and hid.

paras.zh: 他的舍人们看不下去，一起劝他：「臣所以去親戚而事君者，徒慕君之髙義也。」我们离开亲人来侍奉您，是仰慕您的高义；如今您与廉颇同列，廉君放出那样的话，您却怕成这样、躲个不停，「且庸人尚羞之，況於將相乎」——平常人都觉得丢脸，何况是将相。我们没本事，请允许我们告辞。
paras.en: His retainers could not stomach it, and came to him together to protest: we left our kith and kin to serve you only because we admired your lofty honor. Now you sit in the same rank as Lian Po, he pours out insults, and you cringe and hide, frightened out of all proportion. Even ordinary men would be ashamed of this - let alone generals and ministers. We are not good enough for you; we ask leave to go.

paras.zh: 相如坚决把他们留住，反问一句：你们看廉将军和秦王比，谁更厉害？舍人说，廉将军当然不如秦王。相如说，以秦王那样的威势，我敢当廷呵斥他、羞辱他的群臣，我再没出息，难道单单怕一个廉将军？「顧吾念之，彊秦之所以不敢加兵於趙者，徒以吾兩人在也。今兩虎共鬥，其勢不倶生。」我所以这样做，「以先國家之急而後私讎也」。
paras.en: Lin Xiangru firmly refused to let them leave, and put a question back: how does General Lian compare with the king of Qin? Not his equal, they said. With all the king of Qin's might, said Lin Xiangru, I rebuked him to his face at court and shamed his ministers. Incompetent as I am, would I be afraid of General Lian alone? But consider: the reason mighty Qin has not dared to send its armies against Zhao is only that the two of us are still here. If two tigers fight, the way things stand, they cannot both live. I do this because I put the state's urgent need first and my private enmity second.

paras.zh: 廉颇听说了这番话，「肉袒負荊」，由宾客引路，到相如门前谢罪，说「鄙賤之人，不知將軍寬之至此也」。两人终于和好，成为刎颈之交。当年廉颇东攻齐，破其一军；两年后廉颇又伐齐，攻下幾邑；再过三年，他攻魏国的防陵、安阳，都攻了下来；又过四年，相如也带兵攻齐，到平邑而罢。
paras.en: When Lian Po heard this, he stripped off his shirt, took up a bundle of thorns on his back, and came through guests to Lin Xiangru's gate to apologize: a crude and lowly man, he said, who did not know how far the general's generosity went. In the end the two were reconciled and became friends who would die for each other. That same year Lian Po struck east against Qi and broke one of its armies. Two years on he campaigned against Qi again and took Ji. Three years after that he stormed Wei's Fangling and Anyang. Four years later Lin Xiangru himself led an army against Qi and stopped at Pingyi.

heading.en: How the Way Out Was Built

paras.zh: 值得一提的是廉颇的委屈。他的功劳是攻城野战，相如的功劳在秦廷与渑池；作者认为，两种功劳形态不同，本不好用同一把尺子量。他说相如「素賤人」、羞于居下，一种解释是，他不服的不只是排序，还有出身。还有一种解释是，廉颇计较的不是功劳有无，而是功劳能否被看见——战场胜负可以点数，口舌上的成败要靠人转述。
paras.en: Lian Po's grievance deserves a moment first. His merit was won storming cities; Lin Xiangru's, at the Qin court and at Mianchi. In the author's view, the two kinds of credit have different shapes and are not easily measured with one ruler. He jibed that Lin Xiangru had always been a man of low station and that he was ashamed to rank beneath him; one reading is that what rankled was not only the ordering but the birth behind it. Another reading is that what Lian Po cared about was not whether merit existed but whether it could be seen: a battlefield result can be counted off, whereas success with words depends on someone else retelling it.

paras.zh: 相如的避让也不是单纯的忍。他给舍人的理由不是廉颇不值一提，而是一个盘面判断：「彊秦之所以不敢加兵於趙者，徒以吾兩人在也」——强秦不敢动手，只因为我们两个还在。作者认为，他把争执从谁功劳大，换成了赵国安危系于两人并存。同时，避让用的是称病、让路这类不上台面的动作，原文只记了称病、引车避匿，没有记他公开回应廉颇；一种解释是，这样就没有把对方逼到必须立刻表态的位置。一种解释是，这正是给对方留的台阶：羞辱的话是公开说出去的，化解则不是在朝堂上当众进行的（作者解释），廉颇要回头，不必先当众收回自己的话。
paras.en: Lin Xiangru's yielding was not simple endurance either. The reason he gave his retainers was not that Lian Po was beneath notice, but a judgment about the whole board: the reason mighty Qin has not dared to send its armies against Zhao is only that the two of us are still here. The author's reading is that he shifted the dispute from whose merit was greater to the fact that Zhao's safety rested on both men surviving together. And the yielding itself used offstage moves - pleading illness, turning his carriage aside - and the record notes no public reply to Lian Po. On one reading, that kept the other man from being forced to take a stand on the spot. One reading is that this was precisely the ramp built for a retreat. The insult had been spoken in the open; the undoing did not take place before the court (the author's interpretation), so Lian Po could turn back without first withdrawing his words before an audience.

paras.zh: 同一篇列传里，认错的动作出现过两次。早年缪贤有罪，相如给他出的主意是「肉袒伏斧質請罪」；后来廉颇上门，做的是「肉袒負荊」。两者都是脱去上衣、把身体交出去的姿势。不能断言廉颇知道前一桩事或受其影响（作者提示，非原文所述）。另外，相如答赵王时的那段权衡用的是另一套语言：先说清「曲在趙」还是「曲在秦」，把理亏的一方安排到对方。太史公的评语是「退而讓頗，名重太山」——退让，反而把名望抬到了泰山那么高。
paras.en: Within the same biography the gesture of admitting fault appears twice. Lin Xiangru's advice to Miao Xian was to strip and lie on the block to ask pardon; when Lian Po came to the gate, he came stripped to the waist with thorns on his back. Both are postures of baring the body and handing it over. One cannot say that Lian Po knew of the earlier case or was influenced by it; the parallel is the author's observation, not something the text states. The weighing Lin Xiangru offered the king when he answered him uses a different grammar: first settle where the wrong will lie, with Zhao or with Qin, and arrange for it to fall on the other side. The Grand Historian's verdict: he stepped back and yielded to Lian Po, and his name came to weigh as much as Mount Tai.

paras.zh: 虚构一个场景：一家公司的技术团队里，老工程师带了七八年核心系统，新来的同事凭几次故障处置和几场汇报被提拔到他上面。老工程师在周会上说，他不过会讲话。新同事听到风声，开会从不与他争，排期上也让。组里年轻人替新同事不平，觉得他太软。这个局面和朝堂上那两位的区别只在道具：没有马车，只有会议纪要。
paras.en: Take an invented scene. On a company's engineering team, the veteran who has kept the core system alive for seven or eight years watches a newcomer promoted above him on the strength of a few incident recoveries and a handful of status reviews. At the weekly meeting the old engineer mutters that his rival is nothing but a talker. The newcomer hears about it and never argues with him, conceding even on scheduling. The younger members of the team feel he is being far too soft. The only difference from that ancient court is the furniture: no carriages, only meeting minutes.

paras.zh: 另一个虚构场景：一位员工把一个重要客户的项目搞砸了，第一反应是赶紧接下竞争对手抛来的邀请一走了之。一位老同事拦住他：对方愿意要你，是因为你在这里有分量；你一走，这份分量就没了，人家未必还会留你。不如回去，当面把错认了，把补救方案摆出来。这和当年相如劝缪贤的理路一样，只是没有斧质。
paras.en: Another invented scene. An employee has botched a project for an important client, and the first impulse is to take up a rival firm's standing offer and walk away. An older colleague stops them: that firm wants you because of the weight you carry here; leave, and the weight goes with you, and they may not keep you for long. Better to go back, own the mistake face to face, and put a plan for repairing it on the table. It is the same reasoning Lin Xiangru once gave Miao Xian, minus the axe and the block.

paras.zh: 需要说明的不确定性：本文所据材料只有司马迁《廉颇蔺相如列传》一篇，其中的对话是史书的记述，未必是逐字实录；负荆请罪的细节——袒身、背荆条、由宾客引见——在本篇的证据中没有其他材料可以核对。文中对原文未写的人物心理所作的推断，作者尽量以“一种解释是”“作者认为”标明为解释。年份只用原文的「趙惠文王時」这类说法，不换算公元年。
paras.en: The uncertainty to flag: the only material this piece draws on is Sima Qian's biography of Lian Po and Lin Xiangru. The speeches there are a historian's record and need not be verbatim transcripts, and the details of the thorn apology - the bared body, the bundle of thorns, the arrival by way of guests - cannot be checked against any other material in this piece's evidence. Where the piece infers a figure's inner thoughts beyond what the original text says, the author tries to mark such claims as one reading or as the author's inference. Dates stay in the source's own terms, such as in the time of King Huiwen of Zhao, rather than being converted into years before the common era.

paras.zh: 还要说，作者认为，一次认错未必改变了廉颇的脾气。后来赵孝成王去世，悼襄王即位，派乐乘去替代廉颇，廉颇怒而攻乐乘，乐乘跑掉，廉颇便投奔魏国大梁。另据记载，他自长平免归失势时门客散尽，复用为将时门客又回来，门客还说「天下以市道交」，有势就来、无势就走本是常理。把这些放在一起，不是要给谁下道德评语，只是想提示：相如门前那次负荆谢罪见于本篇《史记》记载，但一种解释是，它未必把一个人从此改写。
paras.en: The author's reading is that one apology did not necessarily remake Lian Po's temper. When King Xiaocheng of Zhao died, his successor King Daoxiang sent Le Cheng to replace Lian Po; Lian Po, enraged, attacked Le Cheng, who fled, and Lian Po then went over to Daliang in Wei. According to another passage, when he was dismissed after Changping and lost power, his retainers had all left, and when he was made a general again they came back; one of them told him that the world conducts its friendships on market terms (in translation): people come when you have power and leave when you do not. None of this is a moral verdict on anyone. It is only meant to note that the apology at Lin Xiangru's gate is recorded in this chapter of the Shiji, though on one reading it need not have rewritten the man from that day on.

scenario.zh: 两位长期合作的伙伴因一次公开场合的难听话闹僵：说错话的一方碍于面子不肯先开口，被冒犯的一方在等一个说法，团队因此分成两边，正事停摆。
scenario.en: Two partners who have long worked together fall out after one of them says something unkind in public. The one who misspoke will not speak first, because of face; the one who was offended is waiting for an explanation. The team splits into two camps and the actual work grinds to a halt.

question.zh: 谁先开口、开口说什么，才算既认了错又不失分寸？如果非得借第三方才能见面，这个中间人该是谁、该做什么、又不该做什么？（作者提出）
question.en: Who speaks first, and what should they say, so that a wrong is admitted without the speaker losing his footing? And if a third party is required to bring the two together, who should that go-between be, and what should - and should not - be asked of them? (raised by the author)

assumptions.zh:
双方接下来仍需合作，谁也离不开谁
难听话是当众说的，若道歉也要求当众完成，等于逼对方当场表态
说错话的一方确实有可被看见的功劳，他的委屈有依据
assumptions.en:
The two sides still have to work together afterwards; neither can do without the other
The hurtful words were said in public, so demanding a public apology would amount to forcing a public recantation on the spot
The one who misspoke does have visible credit to his name; his grievance is not groundless

steps.zh:
先找出两人的共同依赖：接下来要一起扛的那件事是什么，把话题从功劳排序挪到共同风险
由双方都信得过的第三方出面约私下见面，不要求任何人在公开场合低头
被冒犯的一方先说明自己在意的是哪句话、哪件事，而不是要求对方全面认错
说错话的一方就那句话认错，同时讲清自己当时的依据（功劳、年头），让委屈留在台面上
用一件共同的小事收尾，让关系回到做事上
steps.en:
Start by finding the shared dependency: what is the hard thing the two must carry together next? Move the conversation from ranking merit to shared risk
Have a third party both sides trust arrange a private meeting, with no one required to bow in public
The offended side states first which specific remark or incident he cares about, rather than demanding a full confession
The one who misspoke apologizes for that remark while making his own basis at the time - his merit, his years - explicit, so the grievance stays on the table
Close on one small shared task, and put the relationship back to work

alternative.zh: 另一种做法（作者提出）：不安排道歉，而是把两人绑定到同一个目标上，用共同的结果自然覆盖旧怨；代价是那句话始终没被处理，日后可能换个场合复发。
alternative.en: Another approach (raised by the author): stage no apology at all, but tie the two men to a single goal and let a shared result quietly cover the old grudge. The cost is that the remark is never dealt with, and may surface again in some other setting.

uncertainty_note.zh: 本文所据为《史记·廉颇蔺相如列传》单一篇章；对话与负荆细节无法以其他材料互证；凡原文未写的人物心理与动机，均以“一种解释是”“作者认为”标明为解释；缪贤旧事与廉颇请罪的并置仅是作者提示，不代表存在影响关系。
uncertainty_note.en: This piece rests on the single chapter of Sima Qian's biography of Lian Po and Lin Xiangru. The speeches and the details of the thorn-apology cannot be cross-checked against other sources. Where the original text says nothing about a figure's psychology or motive, the piece marks its claims as one reading or as the author's view. The juxtaposition of Miao Xian's old affair and Lian Po's apology is the author's observation only and implies no influence between them.

preheader.zh: 一位不服气的老将、一群想辞职的门客，和一捆荆条。
preheader.en: A resentful general, retainers ready to quit, and a bundle of thorns.

sources.citation: 司馬遷《史記·廉頗藺相如列傳》（维基文库本）

what.zh: 完璧归赵、渑池之会、负荆请罪都在前半篇，不长。
what.en: The jade, the Mianchi meeting and the apology are all in the first half.

episode.action: 廉颇不服蔺相如位在其上，相如避让，廉颇肉袒负荆请罪

length.basis: body + question + example; excludes sources and read-more
